name: Azacitidine + Venetoclax (AML, lower-intensity)

biomarkers.note: Not biomarker-restricted. Azacitidine plus venetoclax is the category 1 lower-intensity option for newly diagnosed AML in patients ineligible for or declining intensive induction. IDH1, IDH2 and FLT3 status guide alternative lower-intensity options (ivosidenib, enasidenib, gilteritinib) but are not required for this regimen. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Acute Myeloid Leukemia v5.2026, AML-4 and AML-E 4 of 14.

treatmentSetting: lower-intensity therapy for AML (intensive induction ineligible or declines)
lineOfTherapy: first-line for newly diagnosed AML in patients not eligible for intensive induction (category 1)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: not a candidate for intensive induction chemotherapy, or declines it (typically older or unfit patients)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v5.2026, AML-4 (Lower Intensity Therapy) and AML-E 4 of 14

drugs.name: Azacitidine

provenance.locator: AML-E 4 of 14 (Lower Intensity Therapy, Azacitidine + venetoclax), regimen line

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Acute Myeloid Leukemia v5.2026, AML-E 4 of 14. Azacitidine 75 mg/m2 SC or IV on days 1 to 7 of each 28-day cycle. Hypomethylating agent; expect myelosuppression.

drugs.name: Venetoclax

provenance.locator: AML-E 4 of 14 (Azacitidine + venetoclax regimen line); ramp-up and TLS measures on AML-J 2 of 4 (Principles of Venetoclax Use With HMA or LDAC)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Acute Myeloid Leukemia v5.2026, AML-E 4 of 14 and AML-J 2 of 4. Venetoclax PO once daily with a mandatory cycle 1 intrapatient dose ramp: 100 mg on day 1, 200 mg on day 2, then 400 mg on day 3 and beyond (steady-state daily dose 400 mg; dosePerUnit is set to VERIFY until the 3-day ramp is structurally encoded, because a flat 400 mg day-1 dose would be a fatal TLS risk). The ramp and tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) measures are specified on AML-J 2 of 4. Days 1 to 28 represents continuous once-daily dosing across the 28-day cycle; venetoclax duration may be shortened in later cycles for recurrent cytopenias (AML-J). Dose adjustment is required with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (AML-J).

supportiveCare: TLS prophylaxis for venetoclax ramp-up (AML-J 2 of 4): reduce WBC to below 25 x 10^9/L with hydroxyurea or leukapheresis before starting; hydration; allopurinol or another uric-acid-lowering agent until TLS risk has passed; inpatient monitoring is strongly recommended during the first cycle through dose escalation; monitor blood chemistries every 6 to 8 hours after each dose increase.
Azacitidine and venetoclax are both myelosuppressive: monitor CBC and support with transfusion and infection prophylaxis per institutional practice.
Venetoclax has clinically important interactions with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and may require dose adjustment (AML-J).
Continue therapy while the disease shows clinical improvement (CR or CR with incomplete count recovery); cycles are not fixed (cycles null).

monitoring: CBC with differential before and during each cycle
blood chemistries (electrolytes, uric acid, phosphate, creatinine) every 6 to 8 hours during cycle 1 venetoclax ramp-up for TLS, then at least daily until TLS risk passes
bone marrow assessment for response (response may not be evident before 3 to 4 cycles of a hypomethylating agent)

doseModificationRules.condition: recurrent grade 3 to 4 cytopenias in remission
doseModificationRules.text: Consider reducing venetoclax duration in subsequent cycles (for example 21, 14, 7 or 5 days) and take breaks between cycles for cytopenias with disease in remission (AML-J). Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: concurrent strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor
doseModificationRules.text: Reduce venetoclax dose per venetoclax prescribing information and AML-J when a strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor is co-administered.

guideline.locator: AML-4 (Lower Intensity Therapy, intensive induction ineligible or declines); AML-E 4 of 14 (Azacitidine + venetoclax: azacitidine 75 mg/m2 SC or IV days 1 to 7 of each 28-day cycle; venetoclax PO once daily 100 mg day 1, 200 mg day 2, 400 mg day 3 and beyond); AML-J 2 of 4 (Principles of Venetoclax Use With HMA or LDAC: ramp-up and TLS measures); category 1 designation on AML-4

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for lower-intensity AML in patients ineligible for or declining intensive induction (unfit or elderly). Complements the existing intensive-induction protocols (aml-7-plus-3-induction, aml-hidac-idac-consolidation, apl-atra-ato) rather than replacing them. Both doses are grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Acute Myeloid Leukemia v5.2026: azacitidine 75 mg/m2 SC or IV days 1 to 7 of each 28-day cycle and venetoclax PO once daily with the cycle 1 ramp (100 mg day 1, 200 mg day 2, 400 mg day 3 and beyond) on AML-E 4 of 14; the ramp and TLS prophylaxis are on AML-J 2 of 4. Because a flat 400 mg day-1 dose would misrepresent the mandatory 3-day ramp (a fatal TLS risk), the venetoclax dosePerUnit is set to VERIFY and listed in verifyFields until the ramp is structurally encoded; azacitidine 75 mg/m2 stays grounded. histology is set to VERIFY (the dosing page does not establish a specific morphologic subtype beyond AML) and treatmentIntent is VERIFY (the guideline does not label curative versus palliative intent for lower-intensity therapy). Core textbook cross-reference is pending; grounding is guideline-layer only. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
